Mrk.9.24.bsb: Immediately the boy’s father cried out, “I do believe; help my unbelief!”
Mrk.9.24.kjv: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

Mrk.8.38.bsb: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
Mrk.8.38.kjv: Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

Mrk.1.27.bsb: All the people were amazed and began to ask one another, “What is this? A new teaching with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!”
Mrk.1.27.kjv: And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine is this? for with authority commandeth he even the unclean spirits, and they do obey him.

Mrk.4.38.bsb: But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. So they woke Him and said, “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?”
Mrk.4.38.kjv: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?

Mrk.15.46.bsb: So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.
Mrk.15.46.kjv: And he bought fine linen, and took him down, and wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre.

Mrk.10.47.bsb: When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Mrk.10.47.kjv: And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, and say, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

Mrk.6.3.bsb: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well?” And they took offense at Him.
Mrk.6.3.kjv: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.

Mrk.10.6.bsb: However, from the beginning of creation, ‘God made them male and female.’
Mrk.10.6.kjv: But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female.

Mrk.10.7.bsb: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife,
Mrk.10.7.kjv: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife;

Mrk.10.8.bsb: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Mrk.10.8.kjv: And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh.

Mrk.12.33.bsb: and to love Him with all your heart and with all your understanding and with all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself. This is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
Mrk.12.33.kjv: And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.

Mrk.15.34.bsb: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
Mrk.15.34.kjv: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

Mrk.15.37.bsb: But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
Mrk.15.37.kjv: And Jesus cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.

Mrk.11.25.bsb: And when you stand to pray, if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well.”
Mrk.11.25.kjv: And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.

Mrk.1.35.bsb: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up and went out to a solitary place to pray.
Mrk.1.35.kjv: And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.

Mrk.14.65.bsb: Then some of them began to spit on Him. They blindfolded Him, struck Him with their fists, and said to Him, “Prophesy!” And the officers received Him with slaps in His face.
Mrk.14.65.kjv: And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say unto him, Prophesy: and the servants did strike him with the palms of their hands.

Mrk.15.28.kjv: And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was numbered with the transgressors.

Mrk.10.32.bsb: As they were going up the road to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking ahead of them. The disciples were amazed, but those who followed were afraid. Again Jesus took the Twelve aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to Him:
Mrk.10.32.kjv: And they were in the way going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus went before them: and they were amazed; and as they followed, they were afraid. And he took again the twelve, and began to tell them what things should happen unto him,

Mrk.10.33.bsb: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles,
Mrk.10.33.kjv: Saying, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests, and unto the scribes; and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the Gentiles:

Mrk.10.34.bsb: who will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him. And after three days He will rise again.”
Mrk.10.34.kjv: And they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit upon him, and shall kill him: and the third day he shall rise again.

Mrk.7.3.bsb: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.
Mrk.7.3.kjv: For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.

Mrk.7.4.bsb: And on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions for them to observe, including the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches for dining.
Mrk.7.4.kjv: And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.

Mrk.5.39.bsb: He went inside and asked, “Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead, but asleep.”
Mrk.5.39.kjv: And when he was come in, he saith unto them, Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth.

Mrk.12.25.bsb: When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.
Mrk.12.25.kjv: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as the angels which are in heaven.

Mrk.1.13.bsb: and He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.
Mrk.1.13.kjv: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.

Mrk.13.27.bsb: And He will send out the angels to gather His elect from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven.
Mrk.13.27.kjv: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.

Mrk.9.4.bsb: And Elijah and Moses appeared before them, talking with Jesus.
Mrk.9.4.kjv: And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.

Mrk.16.5.bsb: When they entered the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side, and they were alarmed.
Mrk.16.5.kjv: And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a long white garment; and they were affrighted.

Mrk.16.6.bsb: But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here! See the place where they put Him.
Mrk.16.6.kjv: And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him.

Mrk.16.7.bsb: But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’”
Mrk.16.7.kjv: But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you.

Mrk.6.6.bsb: And He was amazed at their unbelief. And He went around from village to village, teaching the people.
Mrk.6.6.kjv: And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.

Mrk.4.7.bsb: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.
Mrk.4.7.kjv: And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.

Mrk.4.15.bsb: Some are like the seeds along the path, where the word is sown. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
Mrk.4.15.kjv: And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.

Mrk.4.16.bsb: Some are like the seeds sown on rocky ground. They hear the word and at once receive it with joy.
Mrk.4.16.kjv: And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;

Mrk.4.17.bsb: But they themselves have no root, and they remain for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.
Mrk.4.17.kjv: And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.

Mrk.4.18.bsb: Others are like the seeds sown among the thorns. They hear the word,
Mrk.4.18.kjv: And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word,

Mrk.4.19.bsb: but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
Mrk.4.19.kjv: And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.

Mrk.9.50.bsb: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
Mrk.9.50.kjv: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his saltness, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another.

Mrk.14.72.bsb: And immediately the rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” And he broke down and wept.
Mrk.14.72.kjv: And the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.

Mrk.9.41.bsb: Indeed, if anyone gives you even a cup of water because you bear the name of Christ, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.
Mrk.9.41.kjv: For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because ye belong to Christ, verily I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward.

Mrk.10.21.bsb: Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “There is one thing you lack: Go, sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
Mrk.10.21.kjv: Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.

Mrk.3.29.bsb: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin.”
Mrk.3.29.kjv: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:

Mrk.3.30.bsb: Jesus made this statement because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”
Mrk.3.30.kjv: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.

Mrk.7.21.bsb: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery,
Mrk.7.21.kjv: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,

Mrk.7.22.bsb: greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.
Mrk.7.22.kjv: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:

Mrk.7.23.bsb: All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man.”
Mrk.7.23.kjv: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.

Mrk.14.71.bsb: But he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man of whom you speak!”
Mrk.14.71.kjv: But he began to curse and to swear, saying, I know not this man of whom ye speak.

Mrk.14.58.bsb: “We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’”
Mrk.14.58.kjv: We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.

Mrk.2.7.bsb: “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
Mrk.2.7.kjv: Why doth this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?

Mrk.10.46.bsb: Next, they came to Jericho. And as Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho with a large crowd, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road.
Mrk.10.46.kjv: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimeus, the son of Timeus, sat by the highway side begging.

Mrk.10.48.bsb: Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Mrk.10.48.kjv: And many charged him that he should hold his peace: but he cried the more a great deal, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

Mrk.10.49.bsb: Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” So they called the blind man. “Take courage!” they said. “Get up! He is calling for you.”
Mrk.10.49.kjv: And Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called. And they call the blind man, saying unto him, Be of good comfort, rise; he calleth thee.

Mrk.10.50.bsb: Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.
Mrk.10.50.kjv: And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.

Mrk.10.51.bsb: “What do you want Me to do for you?” Jesus asked. “Rabboni,” said the blind man, “let me see again.”
Mrk.10.51.kjv: And Jesus answered and said unto him, What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? The blind man said unto him, Lord, that I might receive my sight.

Mrk.10.52.bsb: “Go,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you.” And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.
Mrk.10.52.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.

Mrk.8.22.bsb: When they arrived at Bethsaida, some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.
Mrk.8.22.kjv: And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.

Mrk.8.23.bsb: So He took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. Then He spit on the man’s eyes and placed His hands on him. “Can you see anything?” He asked.
Mrk.8.23.kjv: And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.

Mrk.8.24.bsb: The man looked up and said, “I can see the people, but they look like trees walking around.”
Mrk.8.24.kjv: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.

Mrk.8.25.bsb: Once again Jesus placed His hands on the man’s eyes, and when he opened them his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly.
Mrk.8.25.kjv: After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.

Mrk.4.11.bsb: He replied, “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables,
Mrk.4.11.kjv: And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables:

Mrk.4.12.bsb: so that, ‘they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.’”
Mrk.4.12.kjv: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them.

Mrk.6.52.bsb: for they had not understood about the loaves, but their hearts had been hardened.
Mrk.6.52.kjv: For they considered not the miracle of the loaves: for their heart was hardened.

Mrk.7.18.bsb: “Are you still so dull?” He asked. “Do you not understand? Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him,
Mrk.7.18.kjv: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him;

Mrk.12.24.bsb: Jesus said to them, “Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?
Mrk.12.24.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, Do ye not therefore err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God?

Mrk.2.19.bsb: Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them? As long as He is with them, they cannot fast.
Mrk.2.19.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

Mrk.2.20.bsb: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.
Mrk.2.20.kjv: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

Mrk.5.35.bsb: While He was still speaking, messengers from the house of Jairus arrived and said, “Your daughter is dead; why bother the Teacher anymore?”
Mrk.5.35.kjv: While he yet spake, there came from the ruler of the synagogue’s house certain which said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further?

Mrk.5.36.bsb: But Jesus overheard their conversation and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe.”
Mrk.5.36.kjv: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.

Mrk.5.37.bsb: And He did not allow anyone to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
Mrk.5.37.kjv: And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.

Mrk.5.38.bsb: When they arrived at the house of the synagogue leader, Jesus saw the commotion and the people weeping and wailing loudly.
Mrk.5.38.kjv: And he cometh to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.

Mrk.5.40.bsb: And they laughed at Him. After He had put them all outside, He took the child’s father and mother and His own companions, and went in to see the child.
Mrk.5.40.kjv: And they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and entereth in where the damsel was lying.

Mrk.5.41.bsb: Taking her by the hand, Jesus said, “Talitha koum!” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!”
Mrk.5.41.kjv: And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.

Mrk.5.42.bsb: Immediately the girl got up and began to walk around (she was twelve years old). And at once they were utterly astounded.
Mrk.5.42.kjv: And straightway the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment.

Mrk.7.29.bsb: Then Jesus told her, “Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”
Mrk.7.29.kjv: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.

Mrk.7.30.bsb: And she went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone.
Mrk.7.30.kjv: And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.

Mrk.9.23.bsb: “If You can?” echoed Jesus. “All things are possible to him who believes!”
Mrk.9.23.kjv: Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.

Mrk.9.25.bsb: When Jesus saw that a crowd had come running, He rebuked the unclean spirit. “You deaf and mute spirit,” He said, “I command you to come out and never enter him again.”
Mrk.9.25.kjv: When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, saying unto him, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.

Mrk.9.26.bsb: After shrieking and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said, “He is dead.”
Mrk.9.26.kjv: And the spirit cried, and rent him sore, and came out of him: and he was as one dead; insomuch that many said, He is dead.

Mrk.9.27.bsb: But Jesus took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up.
Mrk.9.27.kjv: But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up; and he arose.

Mrk.10.13.bsb: Now people were bringing the little children to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them.
Mrk.10.13.kjv: And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them: and his disciples rebuked those that brought them.

Mrk.10.14.bsb: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and told them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Mrk.10.14.kjv: But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

Mrk.10.15.bsb: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
Mrk.10.15.kjv: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.

Mrk.10.16.bsb: And He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them.
Mrk.10.16.kjv: And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.

Mrk.10.19.bsb: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not cheat others, honor your father and mother.’”
Mrk.10.19.kjv: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Defraud not, Honour thy father and mother.

Mrk.7.9.bsb: He went on to say, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.
Mrk.7.9.kjv: And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.

Mrk.7.10.bsb: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’
Mrk.7.10.kjv: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:

Mrk.7.11.bsb: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is Corban’ (that is, a gift devoted to God),
Mrk.7.11.kjv: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.

Mrk.7.12.bsb: he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother.
Mrk.7.12.kjv: And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;

Mrk.7.13.bsb: Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down. And you do so in many such matters.”
Mrk.7.13.kjv: Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.

Mrk.9.37.bsb: “Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me.”
Mrk.9.37.kjv: Whosoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.

Mrk.13.12.bsb: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.
Mrk.13.12.kjv: Now the brother shall betray the brother to death, and the father the son; and children shall rise up against their parents, and shall cause them to be put to death.

Mrk.9.36.bsb: Then He had a little child stand among them. Taking the child in His arms, He said to them,
Mrk.9.36.kjv: And he took a child, and set him in the midst of them: and when he had taken him in his arms, he said unto them,

Mrk.12.1.bsb: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
Mrk.12.1.kjv: And he began to speak unto them by parables. A certain man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it, and digged a place for the winefat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.

Mrk.12.2.bsb: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
Mrk.12.2.kjv: And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard.

Mrk.12.3.bsb: But they seized the servant, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
Mrk.12.3.kjv: And they caught him, and beat him, and sent him away empty.

Mrk.12.4.bsb: Then he sent them another servant, and they struck him over the head and treated him shamefully.
Mrk.12.4.kjv: And again he sent unto them another servant; and at him they cast stones, and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled.

Mrk.12.5.bsb: He sent still another, and this one they killed. He sent many others; some they beat and others they killed.
Mrk.12.5.kjv: And again he sent another; and him they killed, and many others; beating some, and killing some.

Mrk.12.6.bsb: Finally, having one beloved son, he sent him to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
Mrk.12.6.kjv: Having yet therefore one son, his wellbeloved, he sent him also last unto them, saying, They will reverence my son.

Mrk.12.7.bsb: But the tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
Mrk.12.7.kjv: But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours.

Mrk.12.8.bsb: So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
Mrk.12.8.kjv: And they took him, and killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.

Mrk.12.9.bsb: What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.
Mrk.12.9.kjv: What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.

Mrk.12.10.bsb: Have you never read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
Mrk.12.10.kjv: And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner:

Mrk.12.11.bsb: This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
Mrk.12.11.kjv: This was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?

Mrk.12.12.bsb: At this, the leaders sought to arrest Jesus, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them. But fearing the crowd, they left Him and went away.
Mrk.12.12.kjv: And they sought to lay hold on him, but feared the people: for they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way.

Mrk.2.28.bsb: Therefore, the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
Mrk.2.28.kjv: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

Mrk.14.10.bsb: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them.
Mrk.14.10.kjv: And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went unto the chief priests, to betray him unto them.

Mrk.14.11.bsb: They were delighted to hear this, and they promised to give him money. So Judas began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus.
Mrk.14.11.kjv: And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently betray him.

Mrk.4.26.bsb: Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
Mrk.4.26.kjv: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground;

Mrk.4.27.bsb: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.
Mrk.4.27.kjv: And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.

Mrk.4.28.bsb: All by itself the earth produces a crop—first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.
Mrk.4.28.kjv: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.

Mrk.4.29.bsb: And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
Mrk.4.29.kjv: But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.

Mrk.4.30.bsb: Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?
Mrk.4.30.kjv: And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?

Mrk.4.31.bsb: It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.
Mrk.4.31.kjv: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth:

Mrk.4.32.bsb: But after it is planted, it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.”
Mrk.4.32.kjv: But when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it.

Mrk.15.17.bsb: They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.
Mrk.15.17.kjv: And they clothed him with purple, and platted a crown of thorns, and put it about his head,

Mrk.15.23.bsb: There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
Mrk.15.23.kjv: And they gave him to drink wine mingled with myrrh: but he received it not.

Mrk.15.24.bsb: And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.
Mrk.15.24.kjv: And when they had crucified him, they parted his garments, casting lots upon them, what every man should take.

Mrk.15.25.bsb: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
Mrk.15.25.kjv: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.

Mrk.15.26.bsb: And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Mrk.15.26.kjv: And the superscription of his accusation was written over, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

Mrk.15.27.bsb: Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
Mrk.15.27.kjv: And with him they crucify two thieves; the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.

Mrk.15.29.bsb: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
Mrk.15.29.kjv: And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,

Mrk.15.30.bsb: come down from the cross and save Yourself!”
Mrk.15.30.kjv: Save thyself, and come down from the cross.

Mrk.15.31.bsb: In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!
Mrk.15.31.kjv: Likewise also the chief priests mocking said among themselves with the scribes, He saved others; himself he cannot save.

Mrk.15.32.bsb: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.
Mrk.15.32.kjv: Let Christ the King of Israel descend now from the cross, that we may see and believe. And they that were crucified with him reviled him.

Mrk.15.33.bsb: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
Mrk.15.33.kjv: And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.

Mrk.15.35.bsb: When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.”
Mrk.15.35.kjv: And some of them that stood by, when they heard it, said, Behold, he calleth Elias.

Mrk.15.36.bsb: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
Mrk.15.36.kjv: And one ran and filled a spunge full of vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let alone; let us see whether Elias will come to take him down.

Mrk.15.38.bsb: And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
Mrk.15.38.kjv: And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.

Mrk.9.43.bsb: If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire.
Mrk.9.43.kjv: And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:

Mrk.9.44.kjv: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

Mrk.10.2.bsb: Some Pharisees came to test Him. “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” they inquired.
Mrk.10.2.kjv: And the Pharisees came to him, and asked him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife? tempting him.

Mrk.9.49.bsb: For everyone will be salted with fire.
Mrk.9.49.kjv: For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.

Mrk.7.2.bsb: and they saw some of His disciples eating with hands that were defiled—that is, unwashed.
Mrk.7.2.kjv: And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.

Mrk.7.5.bsb: So the Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus: “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with defiled hands.”
Mrk.7.5.kjv: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?

Mrk.7.6.bsb: Jesus answered them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
Mrk.7.6.kjv: He answered and said unto them, Well hath Esaias prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

Mrk.7.7.bsb: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’
Mrk.7.7.kjv: Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

Mrk.7.8.bsb: You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men.”
Mrk.7.8.kjv: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.

Mrk.7.14.bsb: Once again Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “All of you, listen to Me and understand:
Mrk.7.14.kjv: And when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand:

Mrk.7.15.bsb: Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him; but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him.”
Mrk.7.15.kjv: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.

Mrk.7.16.kjv: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

Mrk.7.17.bsb: After Jesus had left the crowd and gone into the house, His disciples inquired about the parable.
Mrk.7.17.kjv: And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.

Mrk.7.19.bsb: because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated.” (Thus all foods are clean.)
Mrk.7.19.kjv: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?

Mrk.7.20.bsb: He continued: “What comes out of a man, that is what defiles him.
Mrk.7.20.kjv: And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.

Mrk.15.10.bsb: For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.
Mrk.15.10.kjv: For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him for envy.

Mrk.11.23.bsb: “Truly I tell you that if anyone says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen, it will be done for him.
Mrk.11.23.kjv: For verily I say unto you, That whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatsoever he saith.

Mrk.11.24.bsb: Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
Mrk.11.24.kjv: Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.

Mrk.1.15.bsb: “The time is fulfilled,” He said, “and the kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe in the gospel!”
Mrk.1.15.kjv: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.

Mrk.11.22.bsb: “Have faith in God,” Jesus said to them.
Mrk.11.22.kjv: And Jesus answering saith unto them, Have faith in God.

Mrk.16.16.bsb: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
Mrk.16.16.kjv: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.

Mrk.5.28.bsb: For she kept saying, “If only I touch His garments, I will be healed.”
Mrk.5.28.kjv: For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.

Mrk.7.27.bsb: “First let the children have their fill,” He said. “For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
Mrk.7.27.kjv: But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.

Mrk.7.28.bsb: “Yes, Lord,” she replied, “even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
Mrk.7.28.kjv: And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.

Mrk.1.16.bsb: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Mrk.1.16.kjv: Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.

Mrk.1.17.bsb: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”
Mrk.1.17.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.

Mrk.1.18.bsb: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
Mrk.1.18.kjv: And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.

Mrk.1.19.bsb: Going on a little farther, He saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat, mending their nets.
Mrk.1.19.kjv: And when he had gone a little further thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.

Mrk.1.20.bsb: Immediately Jesus called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed Him.
Mrk.1.20.kjv: And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.

Mrk.3.10.bsb: For He had healed so many that all who had diseases were pressing forward to touch Him.
Mrk.3.10.kjv: For he had healed many; insomuch that they pressed upon him for to touch him, as many as had plagues.

Mrk.6.54.bsb: As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus
Mrk.6.54.kjv: And when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,

Mrk.6.55.bsb: and ran through that whole region, carrying the sick on mats to wherever they heard He was.
Mrk.6.55.kjv: And ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.

Mrk.6.56.bsb: And wherever He went—villages and towns and countrysides—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.
Mrk.6.56.kjv: And whithersoever he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.

Mrk.7.25.bsb: Instead, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit soon heard about Jesus, and she came and fell at His feet.
Mrk.7.25.kjv: For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:

Mrk.7.26.bsb: Now she was a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin, and she kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.
Mrk.7.26.kjv: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.

Mrk.7.24.bsb: Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre. Not wanting anyone to know He was there, He entered a house, but was unable to escape their notice.
Mrk.7.24.kjv: And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.

Mrk.9.14.bsb: When they returned to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them, and scribes arguing with them.
Mrk.9.14.kjv: And when he came to his disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them.

Mrk.9.15.bsb: As soon as all the people saw Jesus, they were filled with awe and ran to greet Him.
Mrk.9.15.kjv: And straightway all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to him saluted him.

Mrk.9.16.bsb: “What are you disputing with them?” He asked.
Mrk.9.16.kjv: And he asked the scribes, What question ye with them?

Mrk.9.17.bsb: Someone in the crowd replied, “Teacher, I brought You my son, who has a spirit that makes him mute.
Mrk.9.17.kjv: And one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought unto thee my son, which hath a dumb spirit;

Mrk.9.18.bsb: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”
Mrk.9.18.kjv: And wheresoever he taketh him, he teareth him: and he foameth, and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast him out; and they could not.

Mrk.9.19.bsb: “O unbelieving generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to Me.”
Mrk.9.19.kjv: He answereth him, and saith, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him unto me.

Mrk.9.20.bsb: So they brought him, and seeing Jesus, the spirit immediately threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
Mrk.9.20.kjv: And they brought him unto him: and when he saw him, straightway the spirit tare him; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming.

Mrk.9.21.bsb: Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been with him?” “From childhood,” he said.
Mrk.9.21.kjv: And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.

Mrk.9.22.bsb: “It often throws him into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
Mrk.9.22.kjv: And ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us.

Mrk.9.28.bsb: After Jesus had gone into the house, His disciples asked Him privately, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
Mrk.9.28.kjv: And when he was come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, Why could not we cast him out?

Mrk.9.29.bsb: Jesus answered, “This kind cannot come out, except by prayer.”
Mrk.9.29.kjv: And he said unto them, This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.

Mrk.4.36.bsb: After they had dismissed the crowd, they took Jesus with them, since He was already in the boat. And there were other boats with Him.
Mrk.4.36.kjv: And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the ship. And there were also with him other little ships.

Mrk.4.37.bsb: Soon a violent windstorm came up, and the waves were breaking over the boat, so that it was being swamped.
Mrk.4.37.kjv: And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full.

Mrk.4.39.bsb: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.
Mrk.4.39.kjv: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

Mrk.4.40.bsb: “Why are you so afraid?” He asked. “Do you still have no faith?”
Mrk.4.40.kjv: And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?

Mrk.4.41.bsb: Overwhelmed with fear, they asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”
Mrk.4.41.kjv: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

Mrk.13.19.bsb: For those will be days of tribulation unseen from the beginning of God’s creation until now, and never to be seen again.
Mrk.13.19.kjv: For in those days shall be affliction, such as was not from the beginning of the creation which God created unto this time, neither shall be.

Mrk.11.26.kjv: But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.

Mrk.13.32.bsb: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
Mrk.13.32.kjv: But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.

Mrk.10.18.bsb: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.
Mrk.10.18.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God.

Mrk.12.32.bsb: “Right, Teacher,” the scribe replied. “You have stated correctly that God is One and there is no other but Him,
Mrk.12.32.kjv: And the scribe said unto him, Well, Master, thou hast said the truth: for there is one God; and there is none other but he:

Mrk.10.27.bsb: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God.”
Mrk.10.27.kjv: And Jesus looking upon them saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.

Mrk.14.36.bsb: “Abba, Father,” He said, “all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will.”
Mrk.14.36.kjv: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; take away this cup from me: nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt.

Mrk.13.20.bsb: If the Lord had not cut short those days, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen, He has cut them short.
Mrk.13.20.kjv: And except that the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh should be saved: but for the elect’s sake, whom he hath chosen, he hath shortened the days.

Mrk.16.18.bsb: they will pick up snakes with their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well.”
Mrk.16.18.kjv: They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.

Mrk.12.29.bsb: Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.
Mrk.12.29.kjv: And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord:

Mrk.7.1.bsb: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus,
Mrk.7.1.kjv: Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.

Mrk.8.31.bsb: Then He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and after three days rise again.
Mrk.8.31.kjv: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.

Mrk.14.43.bsb: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
Mrk.14.43.kjv: And immediately, while he yet spake, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.

Mrk.14.44.bsb: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away securely.”
Mrk.14.44.kjv: And he that betrayed him had given them a token, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he; take him, and lead him away safely.

Mrk.14.45.bsb: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
Mrk.14.45.kjv: And as soon as he was come, he goeth straightway to him, and saith, Master, master; and kissed him.

Mrk.14.46.bsb: Then the men seized Jesus and arrested Him.
Mrk.14.46.kjv: And they laid their hands on him, and took him.

Mrk.14.47.bsb: And one of the bystanders drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
Mrk.14.47.kjv: And one of them that stood by drew a sword, and smote a servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.

Mrk.14.48.bsb: Jesus asked the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?
Mrk.14.48.kjv: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Are ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and with staves to take me?

Mrk.14.49.bsb: Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me. But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.”
Mrk.14.49.kjv: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but the scriptures must be fulfilled.

Mrk.14.50.bsb: Then everyone deserted Him and fled.
Mrk.14.50.kjv: And they all forsook him, and fled.

Mrk.14.51.bsb: One young man who had been following Jesus was wearing a linen cloth around his body. They caught hold of him,
Mrk.14.51.kjv: And there followed him a certain young man, having a linen cloth cast about his naked body; and the young men laid hold on him:

Mrk.14.52.bsb: but he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away naked.
Mrk.14.52.kjv: And he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.

Mrk.14.53.bsb: They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes assembled.
Mrk.14.53.kjv: And they led Jesus away to the high priest: and with him were assembled all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.

Mrk.14.54.bsb: Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he sat with the officers and warmed himself by the fire.
Mrk.14.54.kjv: And Peter followed him afar off, even into the palace of the high priest: and he sat with the servants, and warmed himself at the fire.

Mrk.14.55.bsb: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they did not find any.
Mrk.14.55.kjv: And the chief priests and all the council sought for witness against Jesus to put him to death; and found none.
